patient_facts.text: Stomach pain began two weeks ago.
The pain is intermittent; it comes and goes rather than being there all the time.
patient_facts.quote: I don't have the pain all the time. It comes and goes.

patient_facts.text: The pain occurs at least once every day.
During an episode the pain reaches 7/10, and then it can go down to 0/10.
patient_facts.quote: When I have the pain, it is 7/10, and then it can go down to 0.

patient_facts.text: The pain is in the epigastrium (she points to it).
patient_facts.quote: It is here (points to the epigastrium).

patient_facts.text: Eating usually decreases the pain or stops it completely.
patient_facts.quote: Food / usually the pain will decrease or stop completely when I eat

patient_facts.text: Large, heavy, fatty meals, such as pizza, make the pain worse.
patient_facts.quote: Large meals / Heavy, fatty meals, like pizza.

patient_facts.text: Feeling hungry makes the pain worse.
The pain comes back 2 to 3 hours after eating.
patient_facts.quote: but it comes back after 2 to 3 hours.

patient_facts.text: Never had pain like this before.
Sometimes feels nauseated when she is in pain.
patient_facts.quote: Sometimes I feel nauseated when I am in pain.

patient_facts.text: Vomited yesterday, for the first time.
patient_facts.quote: Yesterday I vomited for the first time.

patient_facts.text: The vomit was a yellowish, sour liquid.
patient_facts.quote: It was a yellowish, sour liquid.

patient_facts.text: Takes ibuprofen for her knee arthritis, two pills two to three times a day.
patient_facts.quote: ibuprofen (two pills two to three times a day if asked) / for which I take ibuprofen.

patient_facts.text: Urinary tract infection 1 year ago, treated with amoxicillin.
patient_facts.quote: I had a urinary tract infection 1 year ago, treated with amoxicillin

patient_facts.text: Father died of pancreatic cancer at age 55.
patient_facts.quote: My father died at 55 of pancreatic cancer.
My mother is alive and healthy.

patient_facts.text: Does not smoke or use any other tobacco products.

acting_notes: Please sit up on the bed.
Show pain on palpation of the right upper abdomen that is exacerbated during inspiration.
Point to the epigastrium when asked where it hurts the most.
Give the ibuprofen amount (two pills two to three times a day) only if asked.
Laugh when answering that you are sexually active with your husband.
Patient description: married with four children.
patient_questions: My father was diagnosed with pancreatic cancer. Is it possible for me to develop it as well?

additional_considerations.rationale: The most common cause of chronic dyspepsia, thought to reflect peristalsis disorders; a diagnosis of exclusion after no organic cause is found.
These patients look toxic, with severe diffuse abdominal pain, rebound tenderness and involuntary guarding.
No early satiety, anorexia, weight loss or Virchow node, but symptoms are minimal until late in this rare disease.

source_issues: Gold diagnosis #3 (Gastritis) is garbled: an empty 'History Finding(s):' header is followed by 'Physical &am Finding(s):' and four mixed bullets. Bullets were assigned by meaning: NSAID use, pain associated with food, and nausea/vomiting to history; epigastric tenderness to exam.
Gold #1 history cites 'four children'; this appears only in the raw patient description ('married with four children'), not in the Q/A or the note (note PSH: 2 C-sections).
The raw 'Sample Closure' is unrelated text (a survey about job interviews), and the closure checklist mentions a rectal exam; neither was used.
p024 asks about the rest of the immediate family, but the answer covers only the parents.
annotator_notes: Temporality: facts describing the episodic pattern of the current pain (comes and goes, daily frequency, per-episode severity, return 2-3 hours after eating, nausea during pain) are 'recurrent'; onset, progression, location, quality, radiation, and relieving and aggravating factors are 'current'. Vomiting yesterday (a single event) is 'historical'.

p009 (food relieves) and p012 (eating decreases or stops the pain) are merged into f009; p010 'large meals' and p011 'heavy, fatty meals, like pizza' are merged into f012 to avoid paraphrase duplicates.
p017 'Have your bowel movements altered?' 'No' (topic Diarrhea/Constipation) is split into no diarrhea and no constipation, as in the note HPI.
Stage directions '(points to the epigastrium)', '(laughs)' and '(... if asked)' moved to persona.acting_notes; the ibuprofen dose itself is kept in f026.
The patient description 'married with four children' exists only in raw_opening; kept in persona.acting_notes.
The additional-diagnosis bullet 'Other etiologies' lists five diagnoses; split into one record each.
